questions.question:
Which of the following are properties of ionic compounds?

A. High melting point

B. Soluble in non-polar solvents

C. Conduct electricity in solid state

D. Brittle in nature
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (A) and (D)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement A refers to **High melting and boiling points**. Ionic compounds are composed of a giant **3D crystal lattice** where ions are held together by exceptionally strong **electrostatic forces** of attraction. Overcoming these forces to change the state requires a massive amount of **thermal energy**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• Statement B discusses solubility in **non-polar solvents**. Ionic compounds are **polar** and strictly follow the **like dissolves like** principle. While they dissolve readily in **polar solvents** like **water** (due to ion-dipole interactions), they are generally insoluble in **non-polar solvents** such as **benzene**, **ether**, or **kerosene**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• Statement C describes **electrical conductivity** in the solid state. In solid form, the ions are locked in fixed positions within the **crystalline structure** and are not free to move. Electricity is only conducted in **molten** or **aqueous** states where the **lattice** breaks down, allowing ions to migrate. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• Statement D highlights that these compounds are **brittle**. When a mechanical force is applied, layers of the **lattice** shift, bringing ions of the **same charge** into close proximity. The resulting **strong electrostatic repulsion** causes the crystal to shatter easily. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Ionic Bonding**:

 
 
• Formed through the **complete transfer** of valence electrons from a metal to a non-metal.
 
• Involves the formation of **cations** (positive) and **anions** (negative).
 
• Prominent examples include **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** and **Magnesium Oxide (MgO)**.
 
 
 
• **Solubility and Hydration**:
 
 
• Solubility depends on the balance between **Lattice Energy** and **Hydration Energy**.
 
• **Water** has a high **dielectric constant**, which effectively weakens the attraction between ions, facilitating dissolution.
 
 
 
• **Crystalline Structure**:
 
 
• Ionic solids exist as **regular geometric patterns** rather than discrete molecules.
 
• The specific **coordination number** of an ion depends on the relative sizes of the **cation** and **anion**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true when a beam of white light is incident on a glass prism?

(i) The white light undergoes dispersion.

(ii) The speed of light remains constant when it goes from air into the prism.

(iii) The speed of light decreases as the light goes from air into the prism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement (i) refers to the phenomenon where **white light**, upon entering a **glass prism**, splits into its constituent spectrum of seven colors. This occurs because different colors of light possess different **wavelengths** and travel at different speeds within the glass, causing them to bend at different angles. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• Statement (ii) claims that the speed of light remains constant. In physics, the speed of light is only a constant (approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s) in a **vacuum**. When light transitions from a rarer medium like **air** to a denser medium like **glass**, its velocity must change according to the optical density of the material. ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***
 
• Statement (iii) correctly identifies that the speed of light decreases. **Glass** has a higher **refractive index** (approximately 1.5) compared to air (approximately 1.0003). As per the relation **v = c/n**, where **v** is the velocity in the medium and **n** is the refractive index, a higher index leads to a lower velocity. ***Hence, statement (iii) is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction and Dispersion:**

 
 
• **Refraction** is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent substance into another. This bending is caused by the **change in speed**.
 
• The **Angle of Deviation** depends on the wavelength; **Violet light** deviates the most because it has the shortest wavelength and slows down the most, while **Red light** deviates the least.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index (n):**
 
 
• It is a dimensionless number that describes how fast light travels through the material.
 
• The **Absolute Refractive Index** is calculated as the ratio of the **speed of light in a vacuum** to the **speed of light in the medium**.
 
• For **optical glass**, the index typically ranges from 1.5 to 1.9 depending on the density and composition.

Statement-II: Vanilla extract and onion can be used as olfactory indicators.

options.text: Both statements I and II are true.
Both statements I and II are false.
Statement-I is false but statement-II is true.
Statement-I is true but statement-II is false.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements I and II are true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are specific substances whose smell or odour varies significantly depending on whether they are placed in an **acidic** or **basic** medium. The term 'olfactory' is derived from the sense of smell, making these indicators unique compared to visual indicators like **Litmus paper** or **Methyl orange**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Onion** serves as a reliable olfactory indicator in laboratory settings; when finely chopped onion is treated with a **basic solution** like **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, its characteristic pungent smell is neutralized and cannot be detected. However, in an **acidic medium** like **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, the smell persists. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• **Vanilla extract** is another common example used to distinguish between acids and bases. The pleasant, sweet smell of vanilla disappears when it is added to a **basic solution**, whereas the smell remains unchanged when added to an **acidic solution**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Clove Oil**:

 
 
• Like onion and vanilla, **Clove oil** is a prominent olfactory indicator. Its distinct smell is lost in the presence of a **base** but is retained in the presence of an **acid**.
 
 
 
• **Educational Utility**:
 
 
• Olfactory indicators are extremely important for **visually impaired students** in chemistry laboratories. Since these students cannot observe color changes in indicators like **Phenolphthalein**, they rely on their sense of smell to perform **acid-base titrations**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reaction**:
 
 
• The change in odour occurs because the **hydroxide ions (OH−)** in a base react with the organic compounds responsible for the smell in these indicators, effectively neutralizing the volatile molecules. **Acids (H+)** typically do not destroy these specific aromatic compounds.

questions.question: A train starting from rest reaches a speed of 40 km/h in 10 minutes. What is its final speed in m/s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11.11 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question asks for the conversion of the **final speed** from **kilometers per hour (km/h)** to **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• The given **final speed** of the train is **40 km/h**. The train starts from **rest**, meaning its **initial velocity (u)** is **0**.
 
• To convert a speed value from **km/h** to **m/s**, we multiply the value by the conversion factor **5/18**.
 
• This factor is derived because **1 kilometer** is equal to **1000 meters** and **1 hour** is equal to **3600 seconds** (60 minutes × 60 seconds). Therefore, **1 km/h = 1000 / 3600 m/s = 5/18 m/s**.
 
• Calculation: **40 × (5/18) = 200 / 18**.
 
• Performing the division: **200 ÷ 18 = 11.111...**, which is rounded to **11.11 m/s**.
 
• Although the **time** is given as **10 minutes** (which is **600 seconds**), it is not required for this specific unit conversion of the final speed, but it would be necessary if calculating **acceleration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Units of Measurement**:

 
 
• **Meters per second (m/s)** is the **SI unit** (International System of Units) for velocity and speed, used globally in scientific calculations.
 
• **Kilometers per hour (km/h)** is a common unit used for vehicle speeds and transport systems in most countries.
 
 
 
• **Motion Parameters**:
 
 
• **Acceleration (a)**: Defined as the rate of change of velocity. Formula: **a = (v − u) / t**.
 
• In this context, the acceleration of the train is **(11.11 − 0) / 600**, resulting in approximately **0.0185 m/s²**.
 
• **Uniform Acceleration**: The calculation assumes the train speeds up at a constant rate over the **10-minute** duration.

questions.question: A girl weighing 420 N climbs a rope to a height of 6 m and takes 20 seconds to do it. What is her power output?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**126 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which **work** is done or energy is transformed per unit of time.
 
• The formula for calculating power is **Power (P) = Work Done (W) / Time (t)**.
 
• **Work Done** in this context is the product of the **Force** (weight of the girl) and the **Displacement** (height climbed) in the direction of the force.
 
• According to the given data, the girl exerts a force equivalent to her weight, which is **420 N**, to move a distance of **6 m**.
 
• The total **Work Done** is calculated as: Work = 420 N × 6 m = **2520 Joules**.
 
• The time taken to perform this specific amount of work is **20 seconds**.
 
• By applying the values to the power formula: Power = 2520 J / 20 s = **126 Watts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Watt (W)**:

 
 
• It is the **SI unit** of power, representing one **Joule per second** (1 J/s).
 
• The unit is named after the Scottish inventor **James Watt** for his contributions to the development of the steam engine.
 
 
 
• **Scalar Quantity**:
 
 
• Power is a **scalar quantity** because it only has magnitude and no specific direction.
 
• It describes the **efficiency** or speed of an energy conversion process.
 
 
 
• **Dimensional Formula**:
 
 
• The dimensional representation of power is **[M¹L²T−³]**.
 
• This is derived from Work [M¹L²T−²] divided by Time [T].

questions.question: If A displaces B, and C displaces A, then the order of reactivity is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C > A > B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In chemistry, a **displacement reaction** occurs when a more **reactive element** removes a less reactive element from its compound or salt solution.
 
• The statement 'A displaces B' logically concludes that **A** is more chemically active than **B**. In terms of the **reactivity series**, **A** must be positioned higher than **B** to facilitate this reaction. This establishes the relationship **A > B**.
 
• The statement 'C displaces A' signifies that **C** possesses a higher **oxidation potential** or greater reactivity than **A**. Therefore, **C** is capable of replacing **A** in a chemical bond, establishing the relationship **C > A**.
 
• By synthesizing these two logical inequalities (**C > A** and **A > B**), we derive the complete sequence of reactivity as **C > A > B**.
 
• This hierarchy is a fundamental aspect of **inorganic chemistry**, where elements are ranked based on their ability to lose or gain electrons during **redox reactions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Reactivity Series**:

 
 
• It is an analytical arrangement of metals in descending order of their **chemical reactivity**.
 
• Metals like **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)** are at the top because they react vigorously with water and oxygen even at room temperature.
 
• Metals like **Gold (Au)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Platinum (Pt)** are at the bottom because they are highly stable and resistant to **oxidation**.
 
• The ability of a metal to displace **Hydrogen** from acids is a key metric used to determine its position relative to other elements in the series.
 
• This principle is essential in **extractive metallurgy**, specifically in **carbon reduction** or **electrolytic reduction** processes used to obtain pure metals from ores.

questions.question: Reshma swims back and forth in a 120 m long pool, covering a total distance of 240 m in 1 minute. What is her average velocity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average velocity** is defined as the total **displacement** divided by the **total time** taken for the motion.
 
• **Displacement** is a **vector quantity** that measures the shortest straight-line distance between the **initial position** and the **final position** of an object.
 
• In this problem, Reshma swims in a **120 m** long pool and covers a total distance of **240 m**. This indicates she swims from the starting point to the other end (**120 m**) and returns to the **original starting point** (another **120 m**).
 
• Because she returns to her **starting position**, her final position is the same as her initial position. Therefore, her total **displacement is 0 m**.
 
• The time taken is given as **1 minute**, which is equal to **60 seconds**.
 
• Calculating the **average velocity** using the formula: Average Velocity = Total Displacement / Total Time = 0 m / 60 s = **0 m/s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Average Speed**:

 
 
• Unlike velocity, **speed** is a **scalar quantity** and is calculated using the **total distance** traveled rather than displacement.
 
• In this scenario, the **total distance** is **240 m**.
 
• The average speed would be 240 m / 60 s = **4 m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Scalar vs Vector Quantities**:
 
 
• **Distance** and **speed** are **scalar quantities** as they only have magnitude.
 
• **Displacement** and **velocity** are **vector quantities** as they possess both **magnitude and direction**.
 
• Whenever an object completes a **round trip** and returns to its starting point, its **net displacement** is always zero, regardless of the distance covered.

questions.question: Why is the use of condoms during sexual intercourse recommended?

options.text: Condoms are used to increase fertility in both males and females
Condoms help prevent the transmission of sexually transmitted diseases to some extent
Condoms are required by law to maintain the population balance
Condoms completely eliminate the risk of pregnancy and infections

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Condoms help prevent the transmission of sexually transmitted diseases to some extent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Condoms** are recognized as **barrier contraceptives** that establish a physical wall between partners, preventing the exchange of **bodily fluids** like semen and vaginal secretions.
 
• They are primarily recommended because they significantly reduce the risk of transmitting **Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)**, including **HIV/AIDS**, **Gonorrhea**, **Chlamydia**, and **Syphilis**.
 
• In addition to infection control, they serve as a highly effective tool for **family planning** by preventing **sperm** from entering the uterus, thereby avoiding **fertilization** and **unwanted pregnancy**.
 
• The phrase 'to some extent' is vital because protection is not absolute; **mechanical failure** (breakage or slippage) or contact with infected skin areas not covered by the **condom** can still lead to transmission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methodology and Limitations**:

 
 
• **Contraceptive Efficacy**: While they are very effective, they do not **completely eliminate** risks; according to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, consistent and correct use is required to reach maximum safety levels.
 
• **Fertility**: Condoms are used to prevent conception and do not **increase fertility** in either males or females; in fact, they are the opposite of **fertility treatments**.
 
• **Legal Status**: Usage is promoted for **public health** and **reproductive rights** rather than being a mandatory law for **population balance**.
 
• **Specific Protection**: They are particularly effective against **STIs** spread through discharge, but slightly less effective against those spread through **skin-to-skin contact**, such as **Human Papillomavirus (HPV)** or **Herpes**.
 
• **Materials**: Most are made from **Latex**, though **Polyurethane** or **Polyisoprene** options exist for those with **allergies**.

questions.question: Why are xylem and phloem called “complex permanent tissues”?

options.text: They are temporary in function and disappear after growth.
They contain different types of cells working together for transport.
They consist of only one type of cell for performing a single function.
Their cells can divide and form new tissues.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They contain different types of cells working together for transport**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Permanent tissues** are groups of cells that have lost the ability to divide and have attained a definite shape, size, and specialized function through **differentiation**.
 
• These tissues are termed **complex** because they are composed of **more than one type of cell** that coordinate together to perform a common vital function, unlike **simple tissues** which consist of only one cell type. Hence, the statement that they contain different types of cells working together is correct.
 
• **Xylem** and **phloem** are the primary **conducting tissues** or **vascular tissues** in plants, acting as a plumbing system for nutrient and water movement.
 
• **Xylem** is responsible for the **upward conduction** of water and dissolved minerals from the soil to the leaves and other plant parts.
 
• **Phloem** facilitates the process of **translocation**, which involves the transport of **organic nutrients** (food) synthesized during photosynthesis from the leaves to storage organs and growing regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituents of Xylem**:

 
 
• **Tracheids** and **Vessels**: Tubular structures that conduct water; they are **dead cells** at maturity with thick **lignified walls**.
 
• **Xylem Parenchyma**: The only **living component** of xylem, involved in food storage and lateral conduction of water.
 
• **Xylem Fibres**: Provide mechanical support to the plant body.
 
 
 
• **Constituents of Phloem**:
 
 
• **Sieve Tubes**: Living cells with perforated end walls called **sieve plates**, lacking a nucleus at maturity.
 
• **Companion Cells**: Specialized **parenchymatous cells** that help regulate the pressure gradient in sieve tubes.
 
• **Phloem Parenchyma** and **Phloem Fibres**: Used for storage and structural support respectively.
 
 
 
• **Vascular Bundles**: In the plant body, xylem and phloem are usually organized together into **vascular bundles**, a defining characteristic of **Tracheophytes**.

questions.question: A strong magnetic field produced inside a solenoid can be used to magnetise a piece of soft iron placed inside the coil. The resulting magnet is called a/an __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electromagnet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **solenoid** is defined as a long coil containing a large number of close turns of **insulated copper wire** wrapped in the shape of a cylinder. When an **electric current** passes through it, it creates a **magnetic field** that is nearly uniform inside the coil.
 
• The **magnetic field** produced inside a solenoid is directly proportional to the **current** flowing through it and the number of **turns per unit length**. This field is strong enough to magnetize materials with high **magnetic permeability**.
 
• When a piece of **soft iron** is placed inside the core of a current-carrying solenoid, the iron becomes strongly magnetized. This arrangement is specifically known as an **electromagnet**.
 
• The magnetism of an **electromagnet** is **temporary** and can be controlled; the core loses its magnetic properties as soon as the **circuit is broken** and the current stops flowing.
 
• The **polarity** of an electromagnet can be reversed by changing the **direction of the current**, making it highly versatile for industrial applications like **electric bells**, **cranes**, and **magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)** machines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanent Magnets**:

 
 
• Unlike electromagnets, these are made from **hard magnetic materials** like **steel** or alloys like **Alnico**. They retain their **dipole alignment** even after the magnetizing field is removed.
 
 
 
• **Toroid**:
 
 
• A **toroid** is a solenoid that has been bent into a **circular shape** (like a doughnut). The magnetic field is entirely confined within the **interior space** of the ring, with zero field outside the ideal toroid.
 
 
 
• **Natural Magnets**:
 
 
• These are substances found in nature, such as **Magnetite** (an oxide of iron, **Fe₃O₄**), also known as **lodestone**. They possess **permanent magnetism** but are generally too weak and brittle for practical engineering use.

questions.question: Epithelial tissue primarily functions in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secretion and protection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epithelial tissue** is one of the four basic types of animal tissues that acts as a **protective covering** or lining for the body surface, **internal organs**, and cavities.
 
• The primary function of **protection** is evident in the **skin** (stratified squamous epithelium), which provides a physical barrier against **mechanical injury**, **pathogenic invasion**, and **dehydration**.
 
• The **secretion** function is carried out by specialized cells known as **glandular epithelium**, which synthesize and release substances such as **hormones**, **sweat**, **saliva**, and **digestive enzymes**.
 
• These tissues are characterized by **tightly packed cells** with very little **intercellular matrix**, ensuring they form a continuous sheet that regulates the movement of materials between different compartments.
 
• Apart from secretion and protection, epithelial tissues in the **small intestine** and **kidney tubules** are specialized for **absorption** and **filtration** respectively.
 
• A distinguishing feature of all epithelial tissue is that it sits on a non-cellular **basement membrane**, which separates it from the underlying **connective tissue**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coordination**:

 
 
• This is the fundamental role of **Nervous Tissue**, which uses **neurons** to transmit **electrical signals** and **neurotransmitters** to control body activities.
 
 
 
• **Support**:
 
 
• This is the primary function of **Connective Tissue**, which includes **bone**, **cartilage**, **tendons**, and **ligaments** that provide structural framework and bind organs together.
 
 
 
• **Muscle contraction**:
 
 
• This function is unique to **Muscular Tissue**, which contains specialized proteins like **actin** and **myosin** that facilitate **locomotion** and **posture**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Epithelium**:
 
 
• **Simple Squamous**: Facilitates **diffusion** in the **alveoli** of lungs.
 
• **Cuboidal Epithelium**: Found in **kidney tubules** for **mechanical support** and **secretion**.
 
• **Ciliated Columnar**: Found in the **respiratory tract** to move **mucus** via hair-like **cilia**.

questions.question: Why does the sky appear dark to passengers flying at very high altitudes?

options.text: The air molecules absorb all blue light at that altitude.
Scattering of light is not prominent at such heights.
The path of light is scattered back towards the sun.

questions.solution:

• The **wavelength** (λ) is given as **45 cm**. Converting this into the SI unit of **meters (m)** by dividing by 100 results in **0.45 m**.
 
• The **speed of the wave** (v) is calculated using the fundamental wave equation: **Speed = Frequency × Wavelength**. Substituting the values: **v = 2000 Hz × 0.45 m = 900 m/s**.
 
• The **total distance** (d) the wave needs to travel is **1.8 km**. Converting this to meters (**1 km = 1000 m**) gives a total distance of **1800 m**.

questions.question: Two beakers contain sugar solution of different concentrations. A semipermeable membrane separates them. After some time, the level of solution in one beaker rises while in the other, it falls. Which property of solutions does this experiment best demonstrate, and why?

options.text: Osmosis – because solvent molecules move from the dilute solution to the concentrated solution through the semipermeable membrane
Sedimentation – because sugar crystals settle at the bottom due to gravity
Diffusion – because sugar molecules move freely across the membrane until equilibrium is reached
Evaporation – because water molecules escape from the surface of the solution causing a level difference

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Osmosis - because solvent molecules move from the dilute solution to the concentrated solution through the semipermeable membrane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Osmosis** is a fundamental biological and chemical process characterized by the spontaneous net movement of **solvent molecules** (usually water) through a **semipermeable membrane**.
 
• The movement occurs from a region of **lower solute concentration** (dilute solution/high water potential) to a region of **higher solute concentration** (concentrated solution/low water potential).
 
• A **semipermeable membrane** is a biological or synthetic material that allows only certain molecules, typically the **solvent**, to pass through while obstructing the passage of **solute particles** like sugar.
 
• In this experiment, the water molecules move toward the side with the higher sugar concentration to reach **thermodynamic equilibrium**, causing the solution level to rise in the concentrated beaker and fall in the dilute one.
 
• This process continues until the **hydrostatic pressure** generated by the difference in liquid levels equals the **osmotic pressure** of the solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffusion**

 
 
• Involves the movement of **solute particles** from high concentration to low concentration.
 
• Unlike osmosis, it does not strictly require a **semipermeable membrane** to occur.
 
 
 
• **Sedimentation**
 
 
• A physical process where particles settle at the bottom of a liquid due to **gravity**.
 
• It is primarily used in **water treatment** and does not involve movement across membranes based on concentration.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation**
 
 
• A **phase transition** where molecules at the surface of a liquid gain enough energy to enter the gaseous state.
 
• While it can change liquid levels, it is not driven by **solute gradients** or **membrane filtration**.

questions.question: The M shell can take a maximum of ____ electrons, but in Ca it has _____ electrons. [Atomic Number of Ca = 20]
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18, 8**__.

__
 
• The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in any energy level or shell of an atom is calculated using the **Bohr-Bury formula** 2n², where **n** is the **orbit number**.
 
• For the **M shell**, which is the third energy level, the value of **n is 3**. Substituting this into the formula gives **2 × 3² = 18**. Hence, the maximum capacity of the M shell is 18.
 
• **Calcium (Ca)** has an **atomic number of 20**, indicating it has 20 electrons in its neutral state to be distributed across energy shells.
 
• In the electronic distribution of Calcium, the **K shell (n=1)** holds 2 electrons and the **L shell (n=2)** holds 8 electrons, accounting for 10 electrons.
 
• Although the **M shell** can theoretically hold 18 electrons, the **Bohr-Bury scheme** and the **Octet Rule** dictate that the **outermost shell** cannot contain more than 8 electrons for stability.
 
• Therefore, the remaining 10 electrons of Calcium are split: **8 electrons** fill the M shell, and the final **2 electrons** enter the **N shell**. Hence, in Calcium, the M shell contains 8 electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **K Shell (n=1)**:

 
 
• It is the **closest shell** to the nucleus.
 
• Maximum capacity is **2 × 1² = 2 electrons**.
 
 
 
• **L Shell (n=2)**:
 
 
• The second energy level with a maximum capacity of **2 × 2² = 8 electrons**.
 
 
 
• **N Shell (n=4)**:
 
 
• For Calcium, this is the **valence shell** containing **2 electrons**.
 
• The theoretical maximum capacity for n=4 is **32 electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties**:
 
 
• Because Calcium has **2 valence electrons**, it belongs to **Group 2** of the periodic table and is classified as an **alkaline earth metal**.

• The **First finger** (also known as the **Index finger** or **Forefinger**) represents the direction of the **Magnetic Field**, typically directed from the **North Pole** to the **South Pole**.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of hybridisation in crop improvement programmes?

options.text: To grow crops without using fertilizers or irrigation
To increase the natural mutation rate in crop plants
To produce genetically identical plants through cloning
To combine desirable traits by crossing genetically dissimilar plants

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hybridisation** is a fundamental technique in **crop improvement** that involves the crossing of two or more plants with different **genetic makeups** to produce a progeny called a **hybrid**.
 
• The primary objective of this process is to aggregate **superior traits** from different parents—such as **high yield**, **disease resistance**, **early maturity**, and **nutritional quality**—into a single **genotype**.
 
• It utilizes the concept of **genetic recombination**, where the reshuffling of genes during **meiosis** and subsequent fertilization creates **genotypic variations** that do not exist in the original parental lines.
 
• Hybridisation often leads to **Heterosis**, also known as **hybrid vigor**, where the offspring exhibits enhanced physiological characteristics and **biological efficiency** compared to either parent.
 
• The process typically involves careful **selection of parents**, **emasculation** (removal of anthers), and controlled **pollination** to ensure the desired genetic transfer occurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mutation Breeding**:

 
 
• Unlike hybridisation, this method uses **mutagens** (like **Gamma rays** or chemicals) to induce sudden, inheritable changes in the DNA sequence to create new traits.
 
 
 
• **Cloning and Micropropagation**:
 
 
• This involves **asexual reproduction** to produce **Somaclones**. These plants are genetically identical to the parent, which is the opposite of the genetic diversity aimed for in hybridisation.
 
 
 
• **Types of Hybridisation**:
 
 
• **Inter-varietal**: Cross between two different varieties of the same species.
 
• **Inter-specific**: Cross between two different species of the same genus.
 
• **Inter-generic**: Cross between plants belonging to two different genera, often used to introduce **hardiness** or **stress tolerance**.

• By accumulating solutes, the vacuole facilitates the entry of water via **osmosis**, which generates **turgor pressure** against the **cell wall**. This internal pressure is critical for maintaining the **structural rigidity** and upright posture of non-woody plants.

__
 
• In **1911**, **Ernest Rutherford** conducted the **alpha-particle scattering experiment** by bombarding a very thin **gold foil** (approximately 1000 atoms thick) with high-energy **alpha particles**. Hence, the observation that most particles passed **straight through** the foil was central to his atomic model.
 
• The observation that a **vast majority** (nearly 99%) of the **alpha particles** traveled through the gold foil without any **deflection** or change in direction led to the conclusion that the **atom is mostly empty space**. ***Hence, the statement that the atom is mostly empty space is correct.***
 
• Since these **positively charged** helium ions did not encounter any **electrostatic repulsion** or physical obstruction in their path, it indicated that the **mass** and **positive charge** of the atom were not spread out as previously suggested by the **Plum Pudding Model**. ***Hence, the conclusion regarding the empty nature of the atom is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rutherford's Atomic Model** provided several other groundbreaking insights:

 
 
• **The Nucleus**: A very small fraction of particles were deflected by large angles, and 1 in 12,000 rebounded completely (180°), proving that the **positive charge** and nearly all the **mass** are concentrated in a tiny region called the **nucleus**.
 
• **Nuclear Charge**: Because alpha particles (He²⁺) are positive, their deflection by the center confirmed that the **nucleus is positively charged**, not negatively charged.
 
• **Size Proportions**: Rutherford estimated that the radius of the **nucleus** is about 10⁵ times smaller than the radius of the **atom**, reinforcing the **empty space** theory.
 
• **Electron Orbits**: The model proposed that **electrons** revolve around the nucleus in circular paths, similar to planets revolving around the sun.

questions.question: If the radius of the Earth were to double while mass remains the same, the new value of g would be ___________the original value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-fourth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** on the surface of a planet is calculated using the formula g = GM/R², where G represents the **Universal Gravitational Constant**, M is the **mass of the planet**, and R is its **radius**.
 
• According to the question, the **mass (M)** of the Earth remains constant while the **radius (R)** is doubled, such that the new radius R' = 2R.
 
• By substituting the new radius into the gravitational formula, the new acceleration g' is expressed as g' = GM / (2R)². Squaring the term in the denominator results in g' = GM / 4R².
 
• Comparing the new equation to the original formula (g = GM/R²) shows that the new gravity g' is equal to (1/4) × g. This mathematically confirms that the gravitational pull becomes **one-fourth** of the original value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**:

 
 
• First measured by **Henry Cavendish** in 1798, its value is approximately 6.674 × 10−¹¹ Nm²/kg². It is a **scalar quantity** and remains uniform throughout the universe.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting 'g'**:
 
 
• **Shape of the Earth**: Earth is an **oblate spheroid**; the radius at the **equator** is about 21 km longer than at the **poles**. Consequently, g is **maximum at the poles** and **minimum at the equator**.
 
• **Altitude and Depth**: The value of g decreases as we move **upwards** from the surface (altitude) or **downwards** into the Earth (depth). At the **center of the Earth**, the value of g becomes zero.
 
• **Rotation**: The **centrifugal force** generated by Earth's rotation reduces the effective value of g, specifically at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Inverse Square Law**: Gravity follows an **inverse square relationship** with distance. If the distance from the center of mass doubles, the force of attraction is reduced to 2² or 4 times less.

questions.question: If a conductor has a potential difference of 1 V across its ends and a current of 1 A flows through it, what is the resistance of the conductor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law**, formulated by the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, defines the relationship between voltage, current, and resistance in an electrical circuit.
 
• The law states that the **electric current (I)** flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the **potential difference (V)** across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical formula for this relationship is **V = I × R**, which can be rearranged to find **resistance (R)** using **R = V ÷ I**.
 
• In this problem, the **potential difference (V)** is given as **1 Volt (1 V)** and the **current (I)** is given as **1 Ampere (1 A)**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula: **R = 1 V ÷ 1 A = 1 Ω**.
 
• Thus, the **electrical resistance** of the conductor is exactly **1 Ω**, indicating that for every volt of potential applied, one ampere of current will flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Resistance (R)**:

 
 
• **Definition**: It is the property of a material to oppose the flow of **electric charges** (electrons).
 
• **SI Unit**: The unit of resistance is the **Ohm (Ω)**. One ohm is defined as the resistance of a conductor such that a potential difference of **1 Volt** causes a current of **1 Ampere** to flow.
 
• **Resistivity (ρ)**: While resistance depends on shape and size, **resistivity** is an intrinsic property of the material. Metals like **Silver** and **Copper** have very low resistivity.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance**:
 
 
• **Length (L)**: Resistance is directly proportional to the **length** of the conductor. Doubling the length doubles the resistance.
 
• **Cross-sectional Area (A)**: Resistance is inversely proportional to the **area**. A thicker wire has less resistance than a thinner wire of the same material.
 
• **Temperature**: In metallic conductors, resistance increases with an increase in **temperature** due to more frequent collisions between electrons and metal ions.

questions.question: A body of mass 10 kg is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 10 m/s. How much potential energy will be possessed by the body when it reaches the maximum height? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**500 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The problem is based on the **Law of Conservation of Mechanical Energy**, which states that the total mechanical energy (sum of kinetic and potential energy) of an object remains constant if only conservative forces like **gravity** are acting on it.
 
• The **mass** (m) of the body is given as **10 kg** and the initial **velocity** (u) with which it is thrown upwards is **10 m/s**.
 
• At the moment of projection (ground level), the body possesses maximum **Kinetic Energy** (KE) and zero **Potential Energy** (PE). The formula for Kinetic Energy is KE = (1)/(2)mv² .
 
• By substituting the given values, the initial Kinetic Energy is calculated as: 1/2 × 10 kg × (10 m/s)² = 1/2 × 10 × 100 = **500 Joules**.
 
• As the body rises, its velocity decreases due to the **acceleration due to gravity** (g = 10 m/s²), and its Kinetic Energy is converted into **Gravitational Potential Energy**.
 
• At the **maximum height**, the vertical velocity of the body becomes zero, meaning its Kinetic Energy becomes **0 J**.
 
• According to the conservation principle, the entire initial Kinetic Energy (500 J) must be converted into Potential Energy at this peak point. Hence, the Potential Energy at maximum height is **500 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potential Energy (PE) formula**:

 
 
• Potential energy can also be calculated using the formula **PE = mgh**, where **h** is the height above the reference level.
 
• Using the kinematic equation v² = u² − 2gh, and setting final velocity v = 0 at maximum height: 0 = 10² − 2 × 10 × h, which results in **h = 5 meters**.
 
• Placing this height back into the PE formula: 10 kg × 10 m/s² × 5 m = **500 J**.
 
 
 
• **Units and Measurements**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of energy is the **Joule** (J), named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• One Joule is defined as the work done by a force of one **Newton** acting through a distance of one **meter**.
 
• In terms of base units, 1 J = 1 kg·m²/s².

questions.question: Food chains generally do not extend beyond four trophic levels because:

options.text: of large loss of energy at each level

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**of large loss of energy at each level**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The length of a **food chain** is primarily limited by the efficiency of **energy transfer** between different **trophic levels** in an **ecosystem**.
 
• According to the **Ten Percent Law**, formulated by **Raymond Lindeman** in **1942**, only about **10%** of the energy stored as **organic matter** in one trophic level is passed on to the next.
 
• The remaining **90%** of energy is lost to the environment as **heat** during **respiration**, or consumed during **metabolic activities** like growth, movement, and reproduction.
 
• As a result, the amount of available energy decreases exponentially as one moves up the **trophic hierarchy** (from **producers** to **primary consumers**, then **secondary consumers**, and so on).
 
• By the time the energy reaches the **fourth or fifth trophic level**, the residual energy is insufficient to support a stable population of higher-level **predators**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**:

 
 
• **First Level (Producers)**: Includes **autotrophs** like green plants and **phytoplankton** that convert **solar energy** into chemical energy via **photosynthesis**.
 
• **Second Level (Primary Consumers)**: Comprises **herbivores** that feed directly on producers.
 
• **Third and Fourth Levels (Secondary/Tertiary Consumers)**: Consists of **carnivores** and **apex predators**.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Pyramids**:
 
 
• The **Pyramid of Energy** is always **upright** because energy is lost at every step; it can never be inverted, unlike pyramids of biomass or numbers in specific ecosystems.
 
• **Decomposers**: While **saprotrophs** like fungi and bacteria are essential for **nutrient cycling**, they operate outside the linear sequence of the energy-limited food chain.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why anaerobic respiration releases less energy than aerobic respiration?

options.text: It occurs slower than aerobic respiration.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It partially breaks down glucose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerobic respiration** involves the complete oxidation of **glucose** in the presence of **Oxygen** (O₂). This process breaks the carbon-carbon bonds entirely, converting glucose into **Carbon Dioxide** (CO₂) and **Water** (H₂O), releasing a high amount of energy, typically **36 to 38 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
• **Anaerobic respiration** occurs in the absence of **Oxygen**. In this pathway, **glucose** is only **partially broken down** or oxidized. Because the chemical bonds are not fully disrupted, a significant portion of the energy remains trapped within the organic end-products.
 
• In **yeast** and plants, the partial breakdown results in **Ethanol** and **CO₂** (alcoholic fermentation), whereas in **animal muscle cells** during vigorous exercise, it results in **Lactic Acid**.
 
• From a bioenergetic perspective, anaerobic respiration yields a net gain of only **2 ATP** molecules. This energy is derived solely from the **Glycolysis** stage, as the **Krebs Cycle** and **Electron Transport Chain** cannot function without oxygen acting as the final electron acceptor.
 
• The lack of oxygen prevents the full extraction of high-energy electrons from **NADH** through **oxidative phosphorylation**, which is the most efficient stage of energy production in **mitochondria**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Enzymatic Dependency**:

 
 
• Both aerobic and anaerobic pathways are highly dependent on **enzymes**. For instance, **Glycolysis** requires enzymes like **Hexokinase**, and anaerobic fermentation requires **Lactate Dehydrogenase** or **Pyruvate Decarboxylase**.
 
 
 
• **Rate of Respiration**:
 
 
• While anaerobic respiration is less efficient in terms of energy yield per molecule, it can proceed at a much **faster rate** than aerobic respiration, providing a quick burst of **ATP** when oxygen levels are depleted.
 
 
 
• **Location of Processes**:
 
 
• Anaerobic respiration occurs entirely within the **Cytoplasm** of the cell. In contrast, aerobic respiration starts in the cytoplasm but completes its high-energy yielding stages within the **Mitochondria**.

questions.question: Ethanol and ethanoic acid react in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to form a sweet-smelling compound. Which of the following correctly identifies the reaction type and the role of concentrated H₂SO₄?

options.text: It is a neutralization reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as an acid to neutralize the base.
It is an oxidation reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as an oxidizing agent.
It is an esterification reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as a catalyst and a dehydrating agent.
It is a substitution reaction; H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent to remove water molecules.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is an esterification reaction; H2SO4 acts as a catalyst and a dehydrating agent.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Esterification** is a specific type of organic reaction where a **carboxylic acid** reacts with an **alcohol** to form an **ester** and water as a byproduct.
 
• In the given scenario, **ethanoic acid** (CH₃COOH) reacts with **ethanol** (C₂H₅OH) to produce **ethyl ethanoate** (CH₃COOC₂H₅), a compound famous for its **sweet, fruity fragrance**.
 
• **Concentrated sulphuric acid** (H₂SO₄) plays a dual role in this reaction: it serves as a **Brønsted acid catalyst** by providing protons to activate the carboxylic acid group.
 
• Simultaneously, it acts as a **dehydrating agent**. Since the esterification process is **reversible**, the acid removes the water molecules produced during the reaction.
 
• According to **Le Chatelier's Principle**, the removal of a product (water) shifts the **chemical equilibrium** toward the forward direction, significantly increasing the yield of the ester.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Reactants**:

 
 
• **Ethanol**: A primary alcohol used as a solvent and fuel; it does not behave as a typical inorganic base, so the reaction is not a standard **neutralization**.
 
• **Ethanoic Acid**: Also known as acetic acid, it is a weak organic acid that provides the **acyl group** for the ester.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Reaction Types**:
 
 
• **Neutralization**: This typically involves the reaction between an acid and a base to form an inorganic salt and water (e.g., HCl + NaOH).
 
• **Oxidation**: The oxidation of ethanol using **alkaline KMnO₄** or **acidified K₂Cr₂O₇** would convert it into ethanoic acid, rather than forming an ester.
 
• **Substitution**: While esterification involves an **acyl nucleophilic substitution** mechanism, it is specifically categorized as a **condensation reaction** due to the loss of a small water molecule.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Esters**:
 
 
• Esters are primarily used in the manufacture of **perfumes**, **cosmetics**, and **artificial flavorings**.
 
• They undergo **saponification** when reacted with a base like NaOH to produce **soap** and the original alcohol.

questions.question: What is the formula unit mass of ammonium sulphate (NH₄)₂SO₄?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**132 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **formula unit mass** of a substance is defined as the sum of the **atomic masses** of all atoms in a **formula unit** of a compound. It is calculated in the same manner as molecular mass, but specifically for substances whose constituent particles are **ions**.
 
• The chemical formula for **Ammonium Sulphate** is **(NH₄)₂SO₄**. It consists of two **Ammonium (NH₄⁺)** ions and one **Sulphate (SO₄²−)** ion.
 
• To determine the mass, the atomic masses of the individual elements are required: **Nitrogen (N)** is **14 u**, **Hydrogen (H)** is **1 u**, **Sulphur (S)** is **32 u**, and **Oxygen (O)** is **16 u**.
 
• Calculation for the **Ammonium** part: The formula **(NH₄)₂** contains 2 atoms of Nitrogen and 8 atoms of Hydrogen. Mass = (2 × 14) + (8 × 1) = 28 + 8 = **36 u**.
 
• Calculation for the **Sulphate** part: The formula **SO₄** contains 1 atom of Sulphur and 4 atoms of Oxygen. Mass = (1 × 32) + (4 × 16) = 32 + 64 = **96 u**.
 
• The total **formula unit mass** is the sum of these components: 36 u + 96 u = **132 u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ammonium Sulphate**:

 
 
• It is a **colorless** or **white crystalline** salt, often used as a **synthetic fertilizer** for soil.
 
• It is particularly effective in **alkaline soils** as it releases a small amount of **acid**, lowering the **pH** of the soil while contributing essential **Nitrogen** for plant growth.
 
• In addition to agriculture, it is utilized in the **food industry** as an acidity regulator and in **biochemistry** for the purification of **proteins** through the process of **ammonium sulphate precipitation**.
 
• The compound is produced industrially by reacting **ammonia** with **sulphuric acid**.
